title: 15m liquidation-wick pin bar: volume-backed long lower wick, buy the close above the pin high, 2R or 10 bars

source.title: Pin Bar Trading Strategy (The Right Trader)
source.license: All rights reserved (c) 2026 The Right Trader; rule restated, not copied

rule_summary: Chart 15m, closed bars only; signal at a bar close, fill at the next open. Spot, long only, one position per pair, same numbers on all pairs, no higher-timeframe filter. PIN BAR P: range R = high-low; lower wick = min(open,close) - low >= (2/3)R; close >= low + (2/3)R (body in the top third); R/close >= 1.0% (stop-distance floor so cost stays near 0.3R). ACTIVITY FILTER (volume, fixed): volume(P) >= 1.5 x mean volume of the 20 bars before P. ENTRY: the first of bars P+1 or P+2 that CLOSES above high(P) gives the signal; buy at the next open. If neither closes above high(P), the setup is cancelled. Skip if the stop distance at the fill is above 3%. STOP: low(P), fixed at entry. TARGET: entry + 2 x (entry - low(P)). EARLY EXIT: any 15m close below the pin midpoint (high(P)+low(P))/2. TIME EXIT: close of the 10th bar after entry (2.5 hours). No re-entry on the same pin.
mechanism: The long lower wick is a one-bar probe that failed: a burst of market sells (stop runs and forced liquidations of leveraged longs on perpetual venues, mirrored on spot by arbitrage) hit thin bids, and patient buyers absorbed it within the same 15 minutes. The sellers were price-insensitive, so they paid the spread and the overshoot; the absorbers are paid by the snap-back. The volume rule keeps only bars where a real flush happened. Moves: the stop is at least 1.0% away and the target 2R (2%+); losers are cut at the midpoint (about -0.6R) or by time. With a modest hit rate the average gross move should be near 0.5%, above the 0.30% round trip. Second source on the same pattern: the StockSharp Pinbar Reversal example (doc.stocksharp.com api-examples 0065).
